alignment.note: Greek λαβόντες and Latin apprehendentes are aorist/present participles ('having taken/seizing'); the Syriac ܘܢܣܒܘ is a finite verb coordinated by waw ('and they took'). The Syriac thus paratactically chains the action where Greek and Latin subordinate it as a participial circumstance.

The pronominal object 'him' is expressed as the enclitic suffix -ohi on the Syriac verb ܩܛܠܘܗܝ, whereas Greek αὐτὸν and Latin eum employ a free-standing accusative pronoun; equivalent in sense but morphologically agglutinated in Syriac.

Greek repeats the object pronoun αὐτὸν after ἐξέβαλον, while the Syriac again carries it as the verbal suffix on ܘܐܦܩܘܗܝ; the Vulgate ejecerunt omits any explicit object pronoun, leaving 'him' implied from the prior clause.

Greek uses the single adverb/improper preposition ἔξω and Latin the preposition extra; the Syriac renders the notion with a two-element construction ܠܒܪ ܡܢ ('to the outside, from'), an idiomatic compound prepositional phrase for 'outside of'.

The Vulgate inserts a colon (:) after occiderunt, a punctuational division separating the killing from the casting-out; this editorial pointing has no counterpart in the unpunctuated Greek and Syriac token streams.
